note: Core plan: (1) parity of endpoints shows a maximal trail begun at a positive-degree vertex in an even-degree finite graph must close; (2) deleting a closed trail removes an even number of incidences at every vertex, preserving even residual degrees; (3) choose a closed trail with the maximum number of edges, find an unused edge incident to its vertex set by connectedness, construct a nonempty residual closed trail there, and splice to contradict maximality.

Simplification: choose a trail maximal among all trails, not merely a maximal closed trail. Endpoint parity makes it closed. If it omits an edge, connectedness supplies an unused edge incident to its vertex set; cyclically rotate the now-closed trail to that endpoint and append the one unused edge. The extension may be open, but that already contradicts global trail maximality, so residual parity and splicing are unnecessary in the final proof.
